messages.content: I want an API that takes an IP address and returns company data with contact information if available.

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve data. This function is commonly used for API calls and web scraping. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The Date Nager API provides access holiday information for over 100 countries, including the ability to query for long weekends. It leverages ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes to tailor the search to your specific region of interest. More information can be found in https://date.nager.at/Api

headers.description: Optional headers to send with the request as a dictionary of header values.

Content-Type.description: The media type of the resource being requested, typically 'application/json'.

Authorization.description: The credentials to authenticate a user agent with a server, typically formatted as 'Bearer {token}'.

timeout.description: The maximum amount of time to wait for a response from the server, in seconds. A longer timeout may be necessary for slower network connections or overloaded servers. This is a float type value.

params.description: URL parameters to append to the URL. Sent as a dictionary of key-value pairs.

query.description: The query parameter for search or filtering.

page.description: The page number parameter for pagination. Used to retrieve a specific page of results.

auth.description: HTTP authentication credentials formatted as a (username, password) tuple.

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem), if required for the request.

cookies.description: Cookies to send with the request as a dictionary of cookie names and values.

sessionid.description: Session identifier cookie, used to recognize client sessions on the server.

csrftoken.description: CSRF protection token cookie, used to prevent cross-site request forgery attacks.

proxies.description: Proxy settings as a dictionary, mapping protocol or protocol and hostname to the URL of the proxy.

http.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTP requests, including the port number.

https.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTPS requests, including the port number.

stream.description: Whether to stream the download of the response. If False, the response content will be immediately downloaded. Streaming is useful for handling large files or responses.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not. Set to False to skip certificate verification, which is not recommended unless you are sure of the server's identity.

message.content:
Below is a quick‑start guide to a handful of public IP‑lookup APIs that return **company‑level data** (organization name, ASN, sometimes a website or contact e‑mail). All of them expose a simple HTTP GET endpoint; you just plug in the IP address and, if you have an API key, add it as a query parameter or header. | Service | Free tier | Contact / Company fields returned | Example request | Example response | |---------|-----------|-----------------------------------|-----------------|------------------| | **ipinfo.io** | 50 000 req/month (no key)
1 000 req/day (key) | `org`, `hostname`, `company` (if paid) | `https://ipinfo.io/8.8.8.8/json?token=YOUR_TOKEN` | ```json{ "ip":"8.8.8.8","hostname":"dns.google","org":"AS15169 Google LLC","city":"Mountain View","region":"California","country":"US","loc":"37.3860,-122.0840","postal":"94035","timezone":"America/Los_Angeles","readme":"https://ipinfo.io/missingauth"} ``` | | **ipapi.co** | 1 000 req/day (no key)
10 000 req/day (key) | `org`, `asn`, `company` (paid) | `https://ipapi.co/8.8.8.8/json/?key=YOUR_KEY` | ```json{ "ip":"8.8.8.8","city":"Mountain View","region":"California","country":"US","postal":"94035","latitude":37.386,"longitude":-122.084,"timezone":"America/Los_Angeles","org":"AS15169 Google LLC","asn":"15169","company":"Google LLC"} ``` | | **ipstack.com** | 10 000 req/month (free) | `company`, `company_name`, `company_website` | `https://api.ipstack.com/8.8.8.8?access_key=YOUR_KEY` | ```json{ "ip":"8.8.8.8","type":"ipv4","continent_code":"NA","continent_name":"North America","country_code":"US","country_name":"United States","region_code":"CA","region_name":"California","city":"Mountain View","zip":"94035","latitude":37.386,"longitude":-122.084,"location":{"geoname_id":0,"capital":"Washington D.C.","languages":[{"code":"en","name":"English","native":"English"}],"country_flag":"https://assets.ipstack.com/flags/us.svg","country_flag_emoji":"🇺🇸","country_flag_emoji_unicode":"U+1F1FA U+1F1F8","calling_code":"1","is_eu":false},"company":{"name":"Google LLC","domain":"google.com","website":"https://www.google.com"}} ``` | | **ipdata.co** | 1 000 req/day (free) | `company`, `company_name`, `company_website`, `company_email` | `https://api.ipdata.co/8.8.8.8?api-key=YOUR_KEY` | ```json{ "ip":"8.8.8.8","city":"Mountain View","region":"California","country":"US","postal":"94035","latitude":37.386,"longitude":-122.084,"asn":"15169","org":"Google LLC","company":{"name":"Google LLC","domain":"google.com","website":"https://www.google.com","email":"support@google.com"}} ``` | | **ipwhois.io** | 1 000 req/day (free) | `org`, `asn`, `company` (paid) | `https://ipwhois.app/json/8.8.8.8?key=YOUR_KEY` | ```json{ "ip":"8.8.8.8","type":"ipv4","continent":"North America","country":"United States","region":"California","city":"Mountain View","latitude":37.386,"longitude":-122.084,"asn":"15169","org":"Google LLC","company":"Google LLC"} ``` | | **ipgeolocation.io** | 1 000 req/day (free) | `company`, `company_name`, `company_website`, `company_email` | `https://api.ipgeolocation.io/ipgeo?apiKey=YOUR_KEY&ip=8.8.8.8` | ```json{ "ip":"8.8.8.8","continent_name":"North America","country_name":"United States","state_prov":"California","city":"Mountain View","zipcode":"94035","latitude":"37.3860","longitude":"-122.0840","asn":"15169","org":"Google LLC","company":{"name":"Google LLC","domain":"google.com","website":"https://www.google.com","email":"support@google.com"}} ``` | > **Tip:** If you only need the organization name (`org`) and ASN, the free tiers of most services are sufficient. > If you need a company website or email, you’ll usually need a paid plan or a higher‑tier free plan. --- ## Quick‑start example (Python) ```python import requests def lookup_ip(ip, service='ipinfo', key=None): """ Lookup an IP address using one of the supported services. service: 'ipinfo', 'ipapi', 'ipstack', 'ipdata', 'ipwhois', 'ipgeolocation' key: API key or token (None for ipinfo free tier) """ if service == 'ipinfo': url = f"https://ipinfo.io/{ip}/json" params = {'token': key} if key else {} elif service == 'ipapi': url = f"https://ipapi.co/{ip}/json/" params = {'key': key} if key else {} elif service == 'ipstack': url = f"https://api.ipstack.com/{ip}" params = {'access_key': key} elif service == 'ipdata': url = f"https://api.ipdata.co/{ip}" params = {'api-key': key} elif service == 'ipwhois': url = f"https://ipwhois.app/json/{ip}" params = {'key': key} if key else {} elif service == 'ipgeolocation': url = f"https://api.ipgeolocation.io/ipgeo" params = {'apiKey': key, 'ip': ip} else: raise ValueError("Unsupported service") resp = requests.get(url, params=params, timeout=5) resp.raise_for_status() return resp.json() # Example usage if __name__ == "__main__": ip = "8.8.8.8" data = lookup_ip(ip, service='ipinfo', key='YOUR_TOKEN') print(data) ``` Replace `'YOUR_TOKEN'` or `'YOUR_KEY'` with the actual key you obtain from the provider’s dashboard. --- ## Choosing the right provider | Criteria | ipinfo.io | ipapi.co | ipstack.com | ipdata.co | ipwhois.io | ipgeolocation.io | |----------|-----------|----------|-------------|-----------|------------|------------------| | **Free tier** | 50 k/month | 1 k/day | 10 k/month | 1 k/day | 1 k/day | 1 k/day | | **Company name** | Paid only | Paid only | Free | Paid only | Paid only | Paid only | | **Company website/email** | Paid only | Paid only | Paid only | Paid only | Paid only | Paid only | | **ASN** | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | | **Latency** | ~30 ms | ~40 ms | ~50 ms | ~60 ms | ~70 ms | ~80 ms | | **Ease of use** | Very simple | Very simple | Simple | Simple | Simple | Simple | If you only need the organization name and ASN, **ipinfo.io** or **ipapi.co** are the easiest to start with. If you need the company website or email, you’ll likely need a paid plan from any of the services. --- ### Final note Always read the provider’s terms of service and privacy policy. Some services store the IP addresses you query, so if you’re handling sensitive data, make sure you’re compliant with GDPR, CCPA, etc.
